title: The Sincerity of Ministry and Divine Knowledge
english: God stands helping us, so that we may be bold to remain under his providence through and in him; having slightly stripped away the help from him, he persuaded that it is necessary always to trust in him. For such trust not only guards those living in life, but also brings back those having cast it off, raising them again from the dead. Therefore we rouse ourselves, and we enjoin upon you not to have trust based on a familiar power, so that we do not fall away from life, but let us hope in God, who will vivify us even if we become in death.

And know that, although we had trouble and struggle from the seizing, most heavy affliction, yet the branches stood even unto the heart; for we had the response of death, having judged our own death even unto the thoughts. Having done nothing turbulent... whence also we had a good concept about the necessity of trusting in the one raising from the dead and rescuing from death. To the things set forth, it is fitting the fact that I was troubled and did not speak, and that concerning Job, how he did not sin with his lips against the Lord, despite bitter and fearful things having happened to him.

But it is manifest that the things set forth are not written concerning common living and death; for he says: 'He who rescued from such a great death, and rescues, and will yet rescue, is the one in whom we have hoped' (2 Cor 1:10). For if these things were being said concerning common death, those saying these things would never not die, becoming outside of it according to time, but rather those confirming these things would have died the common death; for they say concerning death that it tears the soul away from eternal life.

In the things set forth, he teaches how truly great and divine gifts are given, of many prayers being sent up for one person receiving (2 Cor 1:11). Therefore also he says that he is rousing us toward goodwill and disposition toward him: 'I was rescued from such a great death by God, being joined with you in your prayer on my behalf, so that the grace coming to us, the ones being afflicted, from many representing persons might be thanked by many' (2 Cor 1:11). For if many were co-workers with the prayer toward the gift that has come to pass, it is following that these same should thank the God who provided (2 Cor 1:12). Our boasting toward God is witnessed by the conscience; and it has been said concerning the conscience that the [one] not receiving...

This boasting, which serves as a witness of our conscience, prepared us to conduct ourselves in holiness and sincerity, not by human instruction, but throughout the whole world, and especially toward you. For the one teaching according to the Gospel does not promise a human instruction, but that which comes from the holy writings, which is sincere because it is an external key. He called the wisdom concerning sensible things 'fleshly,' which the one possessing it does not contain the wisdom of the Spirit, regarding it as folly. It is the custom of the Scripture to call the lessons concerning cosmic and material things 'fleshly'; likewise, the mindset of the flesh is so called, and in the works of the flesh, heresies, sorceries, and idolatries are included. For these things are no longer to be explicitly called 'fleshly' by being named from the sensible flesh; for it has been said concerning the material state, by which the one acting according to the flesh is said to walk, and becomes fleshly having been overcome by sin. Nevertheless, even if we have conducted ourselves in holiness and sincerity in the whole inhabited world, we have nonetheless accomplished this more and more toward you.

You have received to read the Gospels and the Law and the Prophets; we write nothing other than what you read (2 Cor 1:13-14). For just as those are God-breathed, which we engrave in the epistles, so are they. Therefore, you also recognize this very thing, having a partial discussion until the end. But we hope with God to find that you come to full knowledge until the end, that is, perfectly and without fail; for having known us in part, and always receiving an increase in the knowledge of the things known and other theorems by that knowledge which surpasses, you will have a perfect vision, just as we write the same things to Moses and the prophets and the evangelists; for the God who came to them as the Word speaks in us, being no other than Christ. And I am confident that with your disposition being thus, that you boast in us; for you yourselves are our boasting in the day of the Lord, in which he will judge those who are made manifest at his judgment seat. And it is possible for the illumination occurring in the souls by the true light to be a day of the Lord Jesus Christ (2 Cor 1:15-16). By this word I demonstrate that the Corinthians, being benefited, had joy in improving themselves. Therefore, by this, intending again with this purpose...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Dual Nature of Christ's Presence and the Purpose of Knowing Satan's Schemes
english: He appears to have been present with them, passing through Macedonia and turning back again from there to see them, so that he might again rejoice seeing them being helped; for it appears through the words, before the writing of both the letters to them, that he was in Corinth. The same is demonstrated by the statement: 'because I was sparing you, I did not yet come to Corinth' (2 Cor 1:23).

Knowing what was said by the Savior in the promise concerning the not needing to swear, but having an unsearchable word regarding the yes as being yes, and the no as being thus, he seems to be confirming himself here by swearing. And most rightly; for he announces the intention he had toward the Corinthians, and this exists in thought and heart; and since it was likely that those he loved would waver concerning the genuineness of the love toward them, he calls God as witness of the things said upon his own soul, standing over the things lying in secret. For he says: 'I am coming to you desiring you, and when I do not do this, I again spare my concern toward you; for you know that having come previously to your city, I spent a whole year and six months staying there, rejoicing in seeing you advancing daily in the benefit according to Christ. For I certainly laid before you the common teaching and the mystical traditions; for I made this clear in the letter before this one, urging you to hold fast to what you received. And since now I am precisely convinced that certain false teachers are deceiving, setting aside the resurrection from the dead and the abiding of the soul, and moreover turning away the knowledge concerning the indifferent, for this reason I refrained now, so that a certain healing through letters might be available to stay with you. And these things I am writing not as one proclaiming himself master of your faith—for we are working together toward your believing—and since from our instruction you have come to faith, just as we taught, so also we remind you, so that you may remain in the faith in which you achieved success; even if some were struck away by the deceivers, nevertheless I am confident that you have stood in the faith in which you received it, being firm in it.'

He says, 'My joy is the joy of all of you through the good report, and declaring that before it, I say truly that my sorrow is the sorrow of all of you (2 Cor 2:3-4); for it was necessary to sadden...'

He rejoices with the apostle to sympathize with the Corinthians, so that those rejoicing may rejoice together. Because I write these things from a sincere disposition, he says, know that through much affliction and pressure of heart, through many tears, the letter is being dictated. For I did not desire to subject you to such rebukes, but rather proofs concerning the dogmas of truth and reminders, and rather an exhortation toward perfect virtue.

This has a dual meaning in the one in the face of Christ (2 Cor 2:10-11). For it is shown either in the face, that is, before and seeing Christ, but also in bearing the face of Christ, having been forgiven, knowing that He Himself, judging that all things for blessedness should be granted, has arrived in life. Therefore, bearing the face—for I desire to imitate Him and to be conformed to Him—I consented to the sin of the one who repented; whence also I am encouraged to be of that opinion. For one must not be ignorant of the wiles of Satan, who, as in former times when fornication was occurring, wished to increase the harm, he was arranging the unfeeling state, so that the one caught in evil would not mourn; but now he has persuaded that there should be compassion toward the one ceasing from evil, so that through this he might also destroy you, the arrogant and the proud, against him. But see, lest anyone, awaiting the will of the apostle, should have the knowledge of satanic thoughts be a vain glory—for such a thing is most harmful, but rather beneficial—for knowing the thought and the choice does not do evil, but rather the choosing does. Therefore, do not neglect also those who are choosing to expose the deceivers, knowing the things of their deception; we are not rebuked, but rather we fully accept them; for it is not the knowing, but the choosing, that makes bad things evil. We know, therefore, the thoughts of Satan, not so that we may act according to them, but so that, not being deceived, we may not be ensnared.

It happened to him that the transition from Troas to Macedonia was through a vision (Acts 16:9). For in the writing of the Acts of the Apostles it is said that truly a Macedonian man was shown to him in Troas by way of revelation, commanding: 'Having crossed into Macedonia, help us.' He fell silent, writing this letter, having tested with the moderation of judgment whether it was not opportune to say such things about himself, as in the...

title: The Meaning of 'Many' and the Living Letter
english: He will show it to those who follow. For the sake of unconcern, he confesses to God regarding the transition, saying what follows next. But discern what he intends: a great door has been opened to me in the Lord; for perhaps a door of the word is opened by the Lord to those receiving it through divine inspiration, but they do not have a preparation from human art. For God says: 'Enlarge your mouth and I will fill it.' And the wise man has cried out: 'Open your mouth with the word of God,' which means being prepared within by desire and readiness to receive the teaching from God. Perhaps the door of the word is opened when the listeners are ready to receive the instruction.

Because of this, he says, God makes manifest through us the fragrance of the knowledge of Christ in every place, since we are the fragrance of Christ (2 Cor 2:14-16); for just as the partakers, being of His light, are the light of the world, so also, being of the scent, those united to Him are His fragrance. And this fragrant breath is, for some, a scent from death to death, and for others, a scent from life to life. But one must not ask why it becomes a scent from death to death; for it happens to those to whom this occurs according to the appearance, just as healthy food seems to harm those who offer it at an unseasonable time. For those who, being under death, receive that which comes upon them through sin, do not receive the divine knowledge with right judgment, but come from the death of practical sins to the death that follows ungodly thoughts, just as it carries those receiving it with deeds from life to life. For just as a perceptible scent, being contributed toward health and well-being, harms small animals that do not possess its most acute breath, so the divine fragrance also benefits and leads toward health, and rather toward life, those who observe the image and likeness of God—for these are truly humans—while those who are harmed by it are those changing according to the inner man, as they are called allegorically, like those destroying a precious preparation of olive oil, according to Ecclesiastes.

One should not pay attention to those of the heterodox who say that the apostles, teaching in Christ, speak against God the Other, contrary to the Father of the Savior (2 Cor 2:17), which is to say, we speak against Him. But he says many...

Those who deceive through being vulgar. For this word 'many', I say, being homonymous, signifies more; for it is sometimes said instead of 'certain people', as when the Lord says: 'many will say to me in that day' (Matt 7:22); but also instead of those addressed to a few, as in 'many are called, but few are chosen' (Matt 22:14). The word also indicates all people, as in how through the hearing of the one, the many became sinners, as if through the hearing of the one [Adam], the many became sinners (Rom 5:12); for all men are under sin having heard Adam. It also indicates the vulgar, as in the present context: 'let not many teachers be you, brothers'; and it also signifies those who are somehow more numerous, just as 'many are rising up against me, and many are saying to my soul'. In the present expression, we are not as certain people trafficking in the word of God, that is, making it vulgar through cold speech and foolish explanation, but as from sincerity we offer it without guile and purely.

He strikes the Corinthians at rest as if they still do not know the apostolic greatness, asserting: 'we think that having our conscience in agreement, we can say sincerely before God in Christ, let us approach; if not, we are recommending ourselves to you by our letter to you' (2 Cor 3:1-3). Thus what concerns us is manifest, as not recommending you to others, nor others to you; for you yourselves are a letter of Christ, ministered by us, truly written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God (2 Cor 3:2-3). For words are inscribed with ink, but a real and contemplative life is characterized with the Spirit of the living God, as one living according to God by the Spirit having been thus written; for the foolish receive the characters from ink as if they were stone tablets for their souls, but those yielding to agreement with the divine in fleshly hearts, that is, sensible hearts, receive the writing from the living Spirit of God; for they are inscribed three times upon the breadth of the heart, just as God gives laws in the mind, by inscribing them upon the breadth of the heart. Let no one think us being foolish, speaking to ourselves: 'that we can say sincerely before God in Christ' (2 Cor 3:4-6); for thus we are disposed concerning ourselves.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
